title: Imaging and Analysis of OT1 T Cell Activation on Lipid Bilayers
protocol: Prepare cell suspensions in complete RPMMI from the spleen and lymph nodes of OT-I transgenic mice.
Adjust splenocytes to approximately 10^7 cells per milliliter.
Incubate adjusted splenocytes at 37°C for 30 minutes with 0.1 μg/ml SIINFEKL peptide.
Rinse incubated cells three times.
Mix splenocytes and lymph node cells in a 1:1 ratio to stimulate T cells.
If retroviral transduction is required, plate 1 mL of cell mixture per well in a 24-well plate. Otherwise, culture the cells in a T75 flask.
Supplement with fresh media plus IL-2 daily starting two days after stimulation.
Transfect Phoenix cells on the day T cells are stimulated using 5 μg pCL-Eco helper virus plasmid and 15 μg of retroviral vector.
Change the media to fresh complete DMEM for transfection the next day.
Retrovirally infect cells 48 and 72 hours after stimulating the T cells.
Mix supernatants from transfected Phoenix cells with IL-2 and polybrene.
Add 1 ml of mixed supernatant to each well containing T cells and spin at room temperature for 1 hour.
Transfer cells from the plate to fresh media in a T75 flask after the second infection.
Coat two 24-well plates with anti-CD3 (clone 2C11) at 2 μg/ml using 0.5 ml/well.
Make a mix of 3.4x10^7 lymph node cells and 6.6x10^7 splenocytes in 50ml of complete RPMI.
Add anti-CD28 (clone PV-1) at 2 μg/ml to the cell mixture.
Aspirate off the anti-CD3 coating solution from two 24 well plates.
Plate 1 ml/well of cell solution in the 24 well plates.
Transfer cells to fresh 24 well plates after 48 hours and spin-infect with GFP virus or Cre-GFP virus.
Leave one well as a non-infected control for setting up the sort.
Transfer cells from plates to T150 flasks after another 24 hours.
Add 50 ml of R10 with 10 U IL2/ml to bring total volume to 100 ml in each flask.
Prepare cells for sorting by filtering through a 40 μm strainer and resuspending in 5–6 ml.
Prepare 2–3 15 ml collection tubes with 2 ml FCS and 2 ml R10.
Plate the sorted cells at 2x10^6/ml in R10 with 10 U IL2/ml after sorting.
Let the cells rest overnight after sorting.
Ficoll the cells the day after sorting to remove dead cells and debris.
Collect live T cells onto a Histopaque cushion.
Wash collected T cells and resuspend in complete RPMI without phenol red indicator.
Load cells with 1 μM Fura-2 AM in PBS for 20 min at 22°C before transferring to complete RPMI without indicator.
Resuspend 2×10^6 cells in ~0.1 ml of complete RPMI without indicator and add 1 μg Alexa Fluor 568-labeled H57-597 anti-TCRβ for surface TCR labeling.
Incubate labeled cells on ice for 30 min, then wash the cells with complete RPMI.
Hold washed cells until imaging.
Add jasplakinolide to cells on ice to inhibit actin depolymerization.
Transfer cells treated with jasplakinolide to a pre-warmed bilayer well containing jasplakinolide at the same concentration used for cell treatment after 15 min incubation on ice.
For control runs, add DMSO vehicle to cells and treat identically as inhibitor-treated cells.
Add blebbistatin to cells for 30 minutes before addition to a well preloaded with blebbistatin.
Keep blebbistatin–containing media in the dark.
Avoid illuminating cells treated with blebbistatin with wavelengths of light below 540 nm.
Treat control cells with DMSO vehicle in an identical manner to drug-challenged cells.
Mix phospholipids (96.5% PC, 2% DGS-NTA(Ni), 1% Biotinyl-Cap-PE and 0.5% PEG5,000-PE) under a stream of nitrogen.
Dry the mixture overnight under vacuum.
Rehydrate the lipid cakes with PBS to a total phospholipid concentration of 4 mM.
Allow the liposomes to hydrate for one hour at room temperature, mixing occasionally by swirling the flask.
Subject the crude liposome preparations to five freeze-thaw cycles using liquid nitrogen.
Extrude the crude mixture through a 100 nm pore-size polycarbonate filter using an Avestin LiposoFast mini-extruder.
Pass the liposome mixture through the extruder for 10–20 cycles.
Store the liposomes at 4°C between uses.
Clean LabTek II chambered coverglasses with 10 M NaOH for 10 min.
Rinse chambers with 1 M HCl in 70% ethanol for 10 min.
Thoroughly rinse chambers with 18 MΩ water.
Dilute liposomes ten-fold to a final concentration of 0.4 mM with PBS.
Apply 0.25 ml of the diluted liposome mixture to each well of a clean chamber.
After 30 min, rinse excess liposomes by repeatedly filling and removing each well with PBS until 12 ml of PBS has been used per well.
Block bilayers for 30 min by adding an equal volume of 2% bovine serum albumin in PBS (PBS-BSA).
Load streptavidin at a concentration of 5 µg/ml for 30 min in the PBS-BSA solution.
Wash away excess streptavidin.
Dilute his-ICAM and biotinylated pMHC from working stocks into PBS-BSA.
Add diluted proteins to bilayers to achieve desired final loading concentrations.
Rinse bilayers after protein loading at 22°C for 30 min.
Warm bilayers before adding cells.
Load streptavidin in excess relative to pMHC molecules (≥400:1 streptavidin:pMHC).
Prepare working stocks of his-ICAM and biotinylated pMHC monomer at 25 μg/ml in PBS-BSA weekly from frozen stocks.
Store prepared working stocks at 4°C between uses.
Set up bilayers for protein motility analysis using TRITC conjugated streptavidin or Alexa Fluor 488-his-ICAM.
Ensure bilayer setup is identical to that used for T cell synapse imaging.
Scan bilayers in the microscope to assess uniformity qualitatively.
Quantify protein mobility by analyzing lipid bilayers using fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP).
Use a C1si confocal microscope in non-spectral mode for FRAP analysis.
Alternatively, use a Mosaic Targeted Illumination system attached to the TIRF microscope for FRAP analysis.
Select random regions on the bilayer and photobleach them.
Acquire time-lapse widefield images of the bilayer post-bleaching to quantify recovery.
Measure loading of his-ICAM and biotinylated pMHC onto bilayers relative to bone marrow-derived dendritic cells (BMDCs).
Load BMDCs with 100 ng/ml SIINFEKL peptide in complete RPMI at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Rinse BMDCs thoroughly after loading.
Generate bilayer standards by setting up lipid bilayers on 5 μm diameter silica microspheres using the same procedure used for coverslip supported bilayers.
Load the bilayer standards with pMHC or ICAM at various concentrations and wash.
Stain the microsphere bilayer standards and BMDCs for ICAM and SIINFEKL:H-2K(b) using YN1/1.7.4 and 25-D1.16, respectively.
Flow cytometric analysis of the BMDCs and microspheres is performed on any suitable flow cytometer.
Add 10^5 cells in 0.1 ml of complete RPMI without Phenol Red indicator to the 0.5 ml of PBS overlaying the bilayer for imaging live OT1⁺ T cells interacting with the bilayers.
Start acquisition as soon as the first cells tether to the bilayer, typically within 1 minute of addition of cells.
Collect Fura-2 component images consisting of 340/10 nm or 380/10 nm excitation with emission recorded at 520/20 nm, using exposures of 33-66 ms at intervals of 15 s for 20 min.
Locate cells undergoing initial spreading onto bilayers.
Acquire TIRF images at 1 or 2 s intervals for 3 to 5 minutes.
Use exposure lengths of 33 to 100 ms.
Continue imaging until all cells are bound to the bilayers, typically up to 10 to 15 minutes.
For jasplakinolide treated cells, image for 5 min after delivering cells into wells.
Prelabel cells with Alexa Fluor 568-H57-597.
Allow cells to interact with pre-warmed bilayers for 15 minutes.
Fix cells with 1–2% paraformaldehyde on the bench.
Permeabilize cells with 0.1% Triton X-100 for 5 min before staining.
Stain cells with Alexa Fluor 488-phalloidin.
Acquire volumetric microscopy stacks using a spinning disk confocal microscope.
Use a 1.4 NA, 100x PlanApo objective (Nikon).
